design.partition_acceptance_rule: both community-pool row counts >= sample_n_per_side; size only
design.sampling_order: sorted community labels; permute; R1 choice then R2 choice; sort chosen row positions
design.unavailable_policy: null with metric reason; retain split and all other metrics; no replacement
design.summary_missing_policy: available values per metric; always report scheduled/available/unavailable counts
design.selection_hash_encoding: domain + NUL + sorted little-endian uint64 positions

limitations: Descriptive point differences only; no confidence intervals, equivalence margins or pass/fail decision.
The selected CHNS reference was previously exposed; this is not independent confirmation or population truth.
Repeated splits reuse one selected cohort and overlap across seeds; they are not independent clinical cohorts.
R1 and R2 are complementary and dependent, while fixed G does not share that partition dependence.
Matching row counts does not make discrepancy distributions exchangeable or match intracommunity dependence.
Community partitioning and row subsampling are not the original survey sampling design.
Symmetric absolute G discrepancy removes reference-role arbitrariness without correcting finite-sample dependence.
The three frozen generated tables remain fixed across splits; this does not quantify generation-model uncertainty.
The real-real distribution is conditional on equally partitioning communities and accepting only size-feasible pools.
Unavailable statistics remain null with reasons and explicit counts; no metric-driven split replacement occurs.
Same-cohort resplits estimate conditional finite-sample variation, not heterogeneity across real populations.
R1 and R2 are complementary and dependent; fixed G does not share that partition dependence. Matching n does not make discrepancy distributions exchangeable.
Community allocation and within-side row subsampling preserve disjointness but are not the original survey sampling design.
Generated rows are IID under the frozen law; matching n does not match real intracommunity dependence.
Three generated draws are one model, not three independent clinical validations.
All current CHNS and generated analyses are exposed developmental results.
No scientific usefulness threshold is learned from these discrepancies; no retroactive pass/fail rule.
